checks.issue: ⚠ TWO COLUMNS, BUT EACH CELL IS ITS OWN VERSE — the opposite of how every two-column page in the roman section was entered. There a row was ONE line of verse split across the gutter, so the row was the unit; here each cell is a COMPLETE numbered duty, and the numbering runs 1-2 across then 3-4, which proves the columns are read across as separate items rather than joined. Ten cells, ten verses. Gutter measured at x 916-1030.
Item 9 prints a Thai gloss in brackets with NO SPACE before it — 'เทศนาบัติ(แสดงอาบัติ)' — where the book normally spaces its brackets. Kept exactly as set.
The closing paragraph is PROSE at full measure with no gutter, against the list above it, so it declares para_layout 'prose'. It also ends with a full stop, which the ten list items do not.
Item 10 ends 'เป็นต้น', and so on — the list is explicitly open-ended at its last item even though the heading counts ten. Kept as printed rather than closed off.

batch_status.paiboon_scan: clean by absence and deliberately so, as on pages 305 to 307. No Paiboon+ was written anywhere in this batch, so none can have drifted.
batch_status.pali_untouched: Trivially confirmed: there is NO Pali on this sheet. Every `pali` and `pali_roman` is empty because the duties are listed in Thai.
batch_status.page_scan: agrees. One row for one page covering verses 1-11, the whole entry. Verse 1 carries the page key and starts the chant. No verse is orphaned and none is claimed twice. No page blocks: the ten duties are verses of the chant the contents names, not page material.
batch_status.notes: One finding, and it reverses a rule this session has applied a dozen times. TWO COLUMNS DO NOT ALWAYS MEAN A ROW IS ONE VERSE. Every two-column sheet in the roman section held one line of verse split across the gutter, so the ROW was the unit; here each cell is a complete numbered duty and the numbers run 1-2 across then 3-4, so the CELL is the unit. The numbering is what settles it, and a page with no numbers would need something else to settle it.
